finding.claim: POST /checkout computes the charge total from client-supplied price and qty with no server-side price lookup or validation, so an authenticated user can pay arbitrary amounts, and negative values may create a credit if payments.charge accepts negatives.

trace.note: Route POST /checkout has no auth guard in this file; relies on upstream middleware setting req.user.
total = sum of attacker-supplied i.price * i.qty.
payments.charge called with req.user.id and the attacker-controlled total.
Charged total echoed back to the client.

finding.guards_checked: None in this file: no catalog price lookup, no array check on items, no type check on price or qty, no sign or bounds check, no server-side recompute. Upstream auth middleware and payments.charge behaviour for negative amounts not present in the repo and unverified.

verdict.guard_found: none. cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty with no catalog lookup, type, sign, or bounds check. cart.js:6 passes that total straight to req.payments.charge. The sibling /checkout-v2 (cart.js:10-17) does look up prices via req.catalog.price(i.sku), but that does not guard /checkout. Upstream auth middleware and payments.charge behaviour are not in the repo.
verdict.reason: cart.js:5-6 charges an amount computed entirely from client-supplied price and qty with no server-side validation, so any caller that reaches the route (which must be authenticated, since req.user.id is read at cart.js:6) can set the charge to an arbitrary value. The negative-amount credit half of the claim is unverified because payments.charge is not in the repo, but the arbitrary-amount part stands on this file alone.

finding.claim: POST /checkout-v2 can produce a NaN total when qty is missing or non-numeric, or a free line item if catalog.price returns null for an unknown SKU, and passes that total to payments.charge.

trace.note: Route POST /checkout-v2; no auth guard in this file.
Price fetched server-side via req.catalog.price(i.sku); unknown SKU result unverified.
Math.floor(non-numeric qty) yields NaN; Math.max(1, NaN) stays NaN, so total becomes NaN. A null price contributes 0.
payments.charge called with NaN or otherwise malformed total.

finding.guards_checked: Server-side catalog price lookup and Math.max(1, ...) clamp (blocks negative-quantity credits). No check for NaN or non-finite total, no SKU existence check. Behaviour of payments.charge with NaN and catalog.price for unknown SKUs not in the repo and unverified.

verdict.guard_found: Server-side price lookup via req.catalog.price(i.sku) (cart.js:13) and the Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)) clamp (cart.js:14). The clamp does not catch NaN: Math.max(1, NaN) is NaN. No finite-total check and no SKU existence check exist in the file. The route has no auth guard in this file (cart.js:10), but req.user.id at cart.js:16 implies upstream auth middleware that is not in the repo.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches cart.js:10, 13, 14 and 16, and nothing in the file rejects NaN (cart.js:14) or a null price, so the mechanics hold; but whether a NaN or zero-priced line causes real harm depends on catalog.price (unknown SKU behaviour) and payments.charge (NaN handling), neither of which is in the repo, so the impact cannot be confirmed. The attacker would be an authenticated user charging themselves, so this is a business-logic/pricing defect rather than a clear security boundary break. Separately, the legacy /checkout route (cart.js:5-6) takes client-supplied price and qty with no server-side pricing or clamp, which is a stronger case but outside this candidate.
